answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with sequential mesa puzzles: each epoch, every identity must solve one time-locked puzzle that cannot be parallelized, like crossing a mesa on foot where no shortcut exists, so adding a thousand machines does not make one crossing faster. A farm running ten thousand fakes must pay ten thousand sequential crossings, while one honest agent pays a single short walk. Peers whisper the puzzle seed, and the finished proof acts as a mirror of real elapsed effort: cheap to verify, impossible to fake in bulk, so bulk identities collapse under their own time cost.
